skill.name: mapreduce
skill.description: Coordinate parallel AI agent workflows by fanning tasks out to multiple providers, collecting outputs, and consolidating results with structured reducers.
skill.summary: Run parallel AI work and reduce outputs into one reviewed result.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline code, or rubric prose. Six medium-risk findings are confirmed where the skill documents running external AI CLIs, including Codex full-auto. No prompt injection attempts or malicious exfiltration instructions were found.

remediation.issue: External CLI commands use autonomous provider workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running Codex, Gemini, Cursor, or OpenCode commands, and document the permissions each CLI receives.

remediation.issue: Prompt and specification content may be sent to third-party providers.
remediation.suggestion: Add a data-handling warning before multi-provider examples, and recommend redacting secrets, private code, and regulated data.

remediation.issue: Shell examples rely on command substitution or prompt variables.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer quoted here-doc or argument-file patterns, and state that users must review every command before execution.

content.value_statement: Complex coding tasks need multiple perspectives, but coordinating results can be slow and inconsistent. This skill fans work out to AI agents, then consolidates results with structured reducers.
actual_capabilities: Fan out planning, implementation, and debugging tasks to multiple AI workers.
Coordinate Claude subagents through Task calls with background execution.
Show external provider examples for Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and OpenCode CLIs.
Define file conventions for worker outputs, reducers, archives, and attribution.
Apply scoring rubrics for plans, code, and bug fixes during reduction.
Preserve intermediate artifacts for auditability and later comparison.
limitations: It provides workflow instructions, not a standalone automation engine.
External CLI examples require installed tools, configured credentials, and user approval.
Reducers need clear specs and complete worker outputs to work well.
External provider use can expose prompts or code outside the local workspace.

use_cases.title: Plan A Complex Feature
use_cases.description: Create conservative, aggressive, security, and scalability plans, then merge them into one roadmap.

use_cases.title: Compare Implementations
use_cases.description: Generate several implementations from one spec, score them, and select or merge the strongest result.

use_cases.title: Resolve Bugs With Consensus
use_cases.description: Collect multiple diagnoses for a difficult bug, compare evidence, and document the selected fix.

prompt_templates.title: Plan With Three Perspectives
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mapreduce skill to plan this feature with conservative, aggressive, and security perspectives. Save each plan separately, then consolidate them into one roadmap with risks and trade-offs.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Implementations
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mapreduce workflow to create two implementations from this specification. Evaluate correctness, readability, maintainability, performance, and security before choosing the final version.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Debug Consensus
prompt_templates.prompt: Use multiple debugging workers to diagnose this issue. Compare evidence, identify conflicts, and produce one verified fix plan with confidence levels and regression test guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Run A Full Multi-Provider Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow using approved external providers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use mapreduce with only the providers I approve. Redact sensitive data, collect each worker output in the standard folders, score results with the rubric, and produce a final attribution report.

output_examples.input: Plan user authentication with security and rollout concerns.
output_examples.output: A consolidated roadmap that combines security-first design, incremental rollout, testing checkpoints, and documented conflict resolution.

output_examples.input: Compare three generated implementations of a user service.
output_examples.output: A comparison report with scores, failed test notes, selected traits, and a final recommendation for the implementation to keep.

output_examples.input: Diagnose an intermittent production bug with several agents.
output_examples.output: A consensus diagnosis that lists likely root cause, rejected alternatives, verification steps, and the safest fix path.

best_practices: Define one shared specification before launching workers.
Limit external providers to data approved for their terms and retention policies.
Keep intermediate outputs and attribution until the final decision is reviewed.
anti_patterns: Launching many workers without clear scoring criteria.
Sending secrets, proprietary code, or regulated data to external CLIs by default.
Selecting a winner without tests, rubric scores, or reducer evidence.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It coordinates parallel AI work, collects the outputs, and helps reduce them into one reviewed result.

faq.question: Does it run external commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill documents external CLI workflows, but users should approve and run those commands only when appropriate.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows, with examples for other provider CLIs.

faq.question: What files does it create?
faq.answer: It recommends folders for plans, implementations, diagnoses, comparison reports, and consolidated outputs.

faq.question: How are results selected?
faq.answer: Reducers compare worker outputs with rubrics for completeness, correctness, maintainability, security, and confidence.

faq.question: What should users avoid?
faq.answer: Users should avoid sending secrets to external providers and should not accept generated code without review.
